givemotion: judge-1 (as A): Most faithful build. The counter rolls correctly through beat 2 (1000 M by 6.53s). The fish draws on stalk first, then body, then teeth (3.38–4.28s), and LIGHT. lights letter by letter (5.0–5.8s). The slider drag lights each card's icon as the handle passes (8.5–9.4s), the toast's check mark draws itself on (12.6–12.9s), and the icon is drawn around the Dot (15.07–15.53s) before a clean end card. Weaknesses: the counter is ghosted and doubled ('1000 M' overlapping itself) as it glides into the phone at 7.2s. The beat-1 stack hugs the top edge (IT'S is about 30 px from the top at 2.7s, inside the 64 px margin). The drop-in stretch reads as a smeary blur overlapping the word above (1.4s, 2.0s), and the cards falling at 11.03s smear into garbled text.

judge-2 (as A): The only one whose counter rolls to 1000 M during beat 2 (3.38–6.53s). The type falls with stretch and overshoot (1.4–2.1s), LIGHT. lights up with the pulses (5.0–5.8s), and the end card is clean (17.1s). Many glitches: broken odometer digits (2.7s), the counter doubled as it moves into the app (7.2s), a readout that says 1000 M while the handle is at 200 (7.88s), two misaligned Lure dots in the hero (11.7s), smeared falling cards (11.03s) and stray letter pieces (15.53s). The fish is a bit chunky.

judge-3 (as B): This one has the most motion energy. Motion blur on the falling words and the slide-ins (1.4s, 2.0s, 4.28s) gives real physics. The corner counter rolls through beat 2 (0652→0999 between 4.7s and 6.1s) and climbs steadily through beat 5. The fish has the best jaw and teeth, and the toast check mark draws itself on (12.6–13.0s). But there are more mistakes: the counter's glide into the app ghosts into a doubled '1888MM' smear (7.2s). The slider readout sits at 1000 M while the handle is still at 200 (7.9–9.0s), so it does not track the drag. A stray glitch mark appears at the left at 15.53s, and at 11.7s the cursor and the lure show as two separate dots next to each other.

judge-4 (as C): Best-drawn, most eerie fish, and the only counter that reaches 1000 M during beat 2. Let down by motion-blur smears and ghosting: doubled text (2.0s, 4.3s), a doubled counter (7.2s), breaking-up cards (11.0s), smears (14.2s) and a stray white fragment (15.5s). The readout already says 1000 M while the handle is at 200 M and doesn't roll during the drag (8.5-9.4s). The block caret covers letters as the tagline types (16.3-16.6s), and at 11.7s the cursor and the lure are two separate dots.

judge-5 (as B): Its hero anglerfish is the most detailed (11.7s), the falling words have motion blur and the end card is polished (17.1s). But the blur leaves smeared, glitchy frames ('HERE.' at 2.02s, 'THEIR OWN' at 4.28s), a doubled, ghosted counter appears at 7.2s, and the readout shows 1000 M while the handle sits at 200 M and does not roll during the drag (8.5–9.4s). Stray white fragments appear at 15.53s, and there is no 6.0s push-in.

judge-6 (as C): The only one whose counter rolls to 1000 M during beat 2 (3.38–6.08s), and it has the richest fish drawing and confident motion-blurred entrances. But the blur smears into artifacts: HERE. lands as a stripy mess (2.02s), THEIR OWN streaks in (4.28s), the dropping cards glitch (11.03s), ANGLERFISH smears as it sinks (14.18s), and stray fragments appear (15.53s). The counter gliding into the app shows as a doubled, ghosted '1000 M' (7.2s); the readout says 1000 M while the handle sits at 200 M and never rolls during the drag (7.88–9.4s); and the oversized semi-transparent caret overlaps the typed tagline (16.3–16.6s). The end card itself is fine, but the piece has the most visible mistakes.
remotion: judge-1 (as B): Good line-art anglerfish with a crescent jaw (5.17–6.08s), a real push-in at 6.08s, a clean phone build (6.97–8.78s), an elegant framed hero panel (11.47s), a nice staggered sink at 14.18s and an icon that draws itself on (15.07s). But the counter is frozen at 0200 M for all of beat 2 and into beat 3 (3.38–7.88s), which breaks a core recurring element. Falling words pass over the stack: HERE. sits on top of IT'S at 2.02s, and DARK/DOWN collide at 1.5s and 2.1s. The lure in the hero illustration stays Biolume until 12.4s, so the Dot match cut is weaker. 'SO THEY MAKE' sits on one line instead of building as separate moves.

judge-2 (as C): The most elegant, eerie fish, with a proper crescent jaw and a well-made hero card (11.7s). A real push-in scales the type past the frame (6.08s), the readout rolls with the drag (9.2–9.4s), and the phone sinks away in a good stagger (14.18–14.62s). Weaknesses: the counter stays at 0200 M through beat 2 (3.38–6.08s), SO THEY MAKE is set on one line instead of building line by line, the teeth arrive late (5.2s), and the hero lure is Biolume instead of Lure until the cursor lands on it (12.4s).

judge-3 (as A): The cleanest and most polished of the three. Beat 1 has words that land with a stretch and the stack sinks (1.3–2.2s). LIGHT. lights up letter by letter in time with the lure pulses (5.0–5.8s). The anglerfish is elegant, the stalk stays attached and the hero illustration is nicely drawn (11.7s). The slider readout rolls 0200→1000 as the handle drags (9.2–9.7s), and the end card is crisp (17.1s). The big brief miss is the counter: it freezes at 0200 M from 2.9s to about 8.5s and never rolls to 1000 M in beat 2. The Dot also slides off the hero lure as the phone sinks (13.7→14.2s), and the toast appears with no visible click on the button (12.4s).

judge-4 (as A): Cleanest and most complete. Type falls with stretch and overshoot and steps back well (1.3-2.2s), the fish draws on around the Dot with believable anatomy (4.7-5.8s), the slider drag lights the right cards with a rolling readout (8.5-10.1s), the card grows into the hero image while the others fall away (11.0s), the toast check draws on (12.6-12.9s) and the end card is polished (17.1s). Biggest miss: the counter stays at 0200 M through all of beat 2 instead of rolling to 1000 M. MAKE doesn't drop in on its own line (3.8s), and the in-app fish is a little plain.

judge-5 (as C): The most faithful delivery: it is the only one with a real 6.0s push-in (6.08s), the fish is elegant with its lure in front of the jaw (4.7–5.8s), the counter glides into the app and the readout rolls in step with the drag (8.3–9.7s), and the card grows into the hero illustration as a clear shared-element move (10.6–11.5s). Weaknesses: the cards fade in late (8.5–8.6s), and around 13.0s a second ringed dot appears above the button while the lure is glowing, which briefly breaks the one-Dot rule.

judge-6 (as B): The most polished and coherent of the three. Clean drop-and-settle type (1.3–2.2s), a fully framed, elegant anglerfish with a proper crescent jaw and teeth (4.9–5.8s), LIGHT. lighting up letter by letter with each pulse, and a clean handover from dot to cursor (6.53–7.2s). The card stack slides into place (8.5–8.7s), and the hero match cut is done right: the hero's lure stays Biolume until the cursor lands on it and turns it Lure (12.1–12.5s). The phone then sinks with a stagger, leaving the dot (14.18–14.62s). Weaknesses: the counter stays at 0200 M through beat 2; 'SO THEY MAKE' is merged onto one line, which loses the separate entrances; the wide type touches the frame edges during the push-in (6.08s); and the hero illustration in its dark inset box reads a little heavy.
hyperframes: judge-1 (as C): Follows the overall structure and has a nice odometer readout in the app (8.8–9.4s), but execution is the weakest. The beat-2 fish is oversized and cropped off the left edge (4.28–6.08s), with the lure dangling far from the mouth. The counter is stuck at 0200 M through beat 2 (3.38–7.42s). LIGHT. is still only 'LIGH' at 5.8s, so the last pulse barely lands before the push. In beat 3 the ANGLERFISH card icon is almost invisible. The cursor sits right on top of the 'LOG SIGHTING' label from 12.1 to 12.9s, hiding it, and at 11.47s the cursor parks on the fish's body rather than the lure. There are faint ghost artifacts on both sides of the frame at 2.7s, and the lower half of the phone is empty in beat 4 (11.7s).

judge-2 (as B): The readout rolls correctly 0200→1000 with the drag, icons light up by depth range (8.8–9.4s), and the toast check draws itself on (12.6–12.9s). The counter stays at 0200 M for all of beat 2 (3.38–6.08s). The fish is cut off by the left edge and its stalk doesn't connect to the head (4.28–6.08s), and HERE. drops right on top of IT'S (2.02s). The cursor parks on the fish's belly (11.47s) and covers the LOG SIGHTING label (12.1–12.9s).

judge-3 (as C): The beat 1 typography is solid (1.3–2.2s), the slider readout rolls in sync with the drag (8.7–9.4s), and the end card is clean (17.1s). The anglerfish is the weakest: in beat 2 its body runs off the left edge of the frame (4.28–6.08s), and the stalk dangles below the jaw with the Dot hanging loose, which reads as awkward rather than eerie. The counter is stuck at 0200 M through beats 2–3. LIGHT. is still not fully lit at 5.8s. The cursor sits over the 'LOG SIGHTING' label and covers the letters (12.1–12.9s), and faint ghost shapes hang around the fading words at 2.7s.

judge-4 (as B): Hits most beats, and the slider readout rolls in step with the drag (8.7-9.4s). The beat-2 fish is weak: the lure stalk isn't joined to the head and the body is cut off by the left edge (4.3-6.1s), and the in-app fish keeps that odd long hook (11.7s). Like A, the counter stays at 0200 M through beat 2. There is a Midwater blob behind the cursor (7.2s), faint stray shapes at 2.7s, and the cursor ring covers the SIGHTING letters on the button (12.1-12.9s).

judge-5 (as A): Clean, close to spec. The Dot keeps its screen position through the handovers (2.9s, 3.4s, 14.6s), the slider readout rolls with the drag (8.8–9.4s) and the end card is tidy (17.1s). There is no 6.0s push-in (the type just vanishes between 6.08 and 6.53s), the counter stays at 0200 M through beat 2 instead of rolling to 1000 M, and the fish is cropped by the left edge of the frame (4.3–6.1s).

judge-6 (as A): Solid beat structure: the words drop with a stretch and land cleanly (1.4–2.2s), the full stop holds its position as it becomes the lure (2.48→2.92s), the dot shrinks into the cursor ring in place (6.53s), and the readout rolls with the slider drag (8.8–9.4s). The end card is clean and holds at 4000 M (17.1s). Weaknesses: the counter stays at 0200 M all through beat 2; the anglerfish is cropped by the left edge (4.28–6.08s); in the hero illustration the lure dot hangs detached from its stalk while the cursor ring drifts over the fish's belly (11.7s); and the cursor sits on top of the 'SIGHTING' label of the button for most of 12.2–12.9s.
